subject.title: bug(agents): nodes tool describe action fails with 'node required' due to schema/implementation mismatch

question: For omitted-node `nodes` `describe`, should OpenClaw default to the current/default node, return list-style discovery output, or keep `describe` target-specific by tightening schema/tool guidance?
rationale: Current main has a real schema/runtime mismatch, but the open fix and issue discussion choose different user semantics for multi-node discovery, so automation should not pick the permanent behavior unilaterally.

options.title: Default-node describe
options.body: Use the existing default-node resolver for no-node `describe`, preserve targeted actions as explicit-node, and add regression coverage for this read-only path.

options.title: Discovery-style describe
options.body: Return node-list/discovery output when `node` is omitted, then keep explicit `node` for detailed `node.describe` calls.

options.title: Target-specific describe
options.body: Keep `describe` requiring a node, but repair model-facing schema/tool guidance so agents do not see omitted `node` as valid for this action.

recommendation.title: Default-node describe
recommendation.body: Use the existing default-node resolver for no-node `describe`, preserve targeted actions as explicit-node, and add regression coverage for this read-only path.

likelyOwner.reason: The central schema and nodes-tool history points to this owner as the best available decision route for the agent tool contract.
